mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS from t-1w to t-0w signals broader leisure recovery and a loosening of voluntary avoidance, which lifts retail and recreation mobility within the next 4 weeks. If park visits keep recovering while residential time eases, RETAIL_REC should rise relative to the last month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -49.9 to -40.4 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 10.4 to 8.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains weak or falls again while RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior 4 weeks, this signal is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops below its recent range and remains near or below -27%, commuting friction suppresses discretionary shopping trips with a short lag, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next 1 to 2 weeks. The mechanism fails if reduced transit is offset by other activity gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -27% and stays there for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -27.1 at t-0w after -27.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -27% for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises over the subsequent 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates fewer daily trips and weaker routine spillovers into shopping districts; together they depress RETAIL_REC over the next month. The effect is strongest when both series stay below their recent averages.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -25.7 to -26.7 while TRANSIT stayed near -27% at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain depressed for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the previous four weeks, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An abrupt improvement in GROCERY_PHARM above the recent trough indicates normalization of essential errands and reduced compliance stress, which typically precedes a broader retail recovery within one week. If this rebound stalls, the retail effect should not appear.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 3 points week-on-week after being below -15%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -17.6 at t-1w to -13.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15% but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During short-term mobility stabilization, a persistently high RESIDENTIAL share signals colder-weather or stay-at-home behavior that displaces shopping outings and keeps RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week mean over the next 4 weeks. The effect weakens if residential time falls.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains positive at 8.0 even after easing from 10.4
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated near or above 8% for four weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises versus the last four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and WORKPLACES move in opposite directions, the leisure rebound does not convert into shopping demand, so RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 2 weeks. The mechanism requires park gains to outpace workplace recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises while WORKPLACES remains below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -49.9 to -40.4 while WORKPLACES stayed negative at -26.7
failure_condition: If PARKS recovers while WORKPLACES remains below -25% and RETAIL_REC still increases over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in TRANSIT combined with weak WORKPLACES mobility implies renewed restrictions or travel frictions that reduce incidental shopping traffic over the next month. The retail effect appears only when both mobility channels remain suppressed simultaneously.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed around -27% and WORKPLACES around -26% through t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain suppressed for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four weeks, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run pullback in PARKS after a brief rebound indicates weather or holiday noise rather than durable reopening, and this usually leads retail mobility to soften over the next week. If parks continue recovering instead of reversing, the signal should disappear.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 5 points after a prior weekly increase
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved sharply from -49.9 to -40.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS reverses downward after a rebound and RETAIL_REC does not weaken in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.
